summary: This is a Snowflake reference page for the STRTOK string function, which tokenizes a string on a set of delimiter characters and returns the requested token by its 1-based number. It explains the syntax, arguments, VARCHAR return type, and usage notes such as NULL handling and never returning an empty token. Several examples show multiple delimiters, out-of-range indexes, empty strings, empty delimiters, and NULL parameters. Website navigation and category boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: Snowflake reference for the STRTOK function, which splits a string on delimiter characters and returns a requested 1-based token.
key_facts: STRTOK(<string> [,<delimiter>] [,<partNr>]) is the syntax of the Snowflake STRTOK function.
STRTOK tokenizes a given string and returns the requested part.
If the requested part does not exist, STRTOK returns NULL.
If any parameter to STRTOK is NULL, the function returns NULL.
The delimiter argument is a set of characters; each character in the delimiter string is a delimiter.
The default value of the STRTOK delimiter is a single space character.
The partNr argument is 1-based, so the first token is token number 1, and its default value is 1.
The data type of the value returned by STRTOK is VARCHAR.
If the delimiter is empty and the string is non-empty, STRTOK treats the whole string as one token.
If the delimiter is empty and the string is empty, STRTOK returns NULL.
STRTOK never returns an empty string as a token, similar to Linux strtok().
SELECT STRTOK('user@snowflake.com.', '@.', 4) returns NULL because the token index is past the last token.
